extracted.intended_audience: UK government departments and policy teams; consultees, stakeholders, and organisations responding to UK public consultations
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for designing and running UK government public consultations and for stakeholders preparing effective consultation responses. Focuses on clarity, purpose, proportionality, targeting, accessibility, engagement, timing, and publication of government responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultations should be clear and concise
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultation documents must use plain English and be easy to understand; questions must be clear and only ask what is necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use plain English; avoid acronyms; be clear what questions are being asked; limit questions to those necessary; avoid lengthy documents when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultations should have a purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultations must be carried out with a defined purpose and intention to use responses to shape policy, and should be held at a formative stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't consult for the sake of it; take responses into account when taking policy forward; consult on policies at a formative stage rather than where there's already a final view.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultations should be informative
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide sufficient information so consultees understand the issues and can give informed responses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give enough information to ensure those consulted understand the issues; enable informed responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultations are part of an engagement process
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultation should be seen as an element of ongoing engagement, not solely as the publication of formal documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not just about formal documents; use new digital tools for informal iterative consultation; consultation is an ongoing process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultations should last for a proportionate time
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultation periods should be proportionate to the nature and impact of the proposal and informed by legal advice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge duration based on legal advice; take into account the nature and impact of the proposal when setting consultation length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultations should be targeted
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and reach out to the full range of people, businesses and voluntary bodies likely to be affected to ensure they are aware and able to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the full range of people, business and voluntary bodies affected; make sure these stakeholders are aware of the consultation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultations should take account of accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure consultations consider groups affected by proposals and use appropriate channels and formats to make participation possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider groups affected by the proposals; use suitable means and channels to ensure accessibility and inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government responses should be timely
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish a government response within a defined timeframe after the consultation closes and meet additional timing requirements for statutory instruments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish within 12 weeks of close (or explain why not possible); for statutory instruments, publish before or at the same time as the instrument is laid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address the specific consultation questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Responses should directly answer the questions posed in the consultation rather than only providing general comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address the specific consultation questions to help officials assess views against the issues they have set out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite evidence proportionate to the proposal's impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Support responses with evidence that is proportionate to the scale and significance of the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite evidence proportionate to the proposal's impact; provide data or sources where appropriate to substantiate claims or recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify the affected community/group you represent
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondents should state who they represent to clarify the perspective and scope of submitted views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the affected community or group you represent (if any) so responses can be understood in context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Note accessibility and equality impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Responses should highlight any accessibility or equality impacts of the proposals so these can be considered in policymaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note accessibility/equality impacts in responses to ensure these considerations are brought to officials' attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit during the formative stage when influence is highest
rubrics_metrics.description: Where possible, engage and respond during the policy's formative stage to maximise the chance of influencing outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit during the formative stage when influence is highest; consultees should aim to contribute while options are still being developed.
